The comparison analyzes the demographic and clinical characteristics of newly diagnosed and prevalent pediatric patients with [[ibd|IBD]] who had hospital contact between October 1, 2023, and September 30, 2024 [^src1]. A total of 198 newly diagnosed patients and 553 prevalent patients are included in the dataset [^src1].

Among the diagnostic categories, [[crohns-sygdom|Crohns sygdom]] is the leading diagnosis for newly diagnosed patients, accounting for 64% (126 patients), compared to 58% (323 patients) among the prevalent group [^src1]. In contrast, [[colitis-ulcerosa|Colitis ulcerosa]] is more common among the previously diagnosed group at 41% (229 patients) than among the newly diagnosed at 36% (71 patients) [^src1]. [[psc|Primær skleroserende kolangitis (PSC)]] represents a marginal outlier in both groups, affecting only 1% of newly diagnosed patients and 0% of prevalent patients [^src1].

The age distribution is heavily concentrated in the 10-17 years age group, which acts as the clear leader, comprising 89% (177 patients) of newly diagnosed children and 93% (514 patients) of prevalent children [^src1]. The youngest age group (0-1 years) is a trailer, representing only 2% of new diagnoses and 0% of prevalent cases [^src1]. Gender distribution is relatively balanced, with boys slightly leading at 53% for new diagnoses and 54% for prevalent cases, while girls account for 47% and 46%, respectively [^src1].

Regarding hospital contact types, physical contacts lead over virtual contacts for both groups. Newly diagnosed patients had 62% physical contacts (1,290) and 38% virtual contacts (806), whereas prevalent patients had a higher proportion of physical contacts at 69% (3,671) and virtual contacts at 31% (1,665) [^src1]. Because this comparison is based on a single dated section covering the 2023-2024 period, no longitudinal trends can be established from this data alone [^src1].

Entities: ibd, crohns-sygdom, colitis-ulcerosa, psc

Summary: Tabellen sammenligner procentvise karakteristika for nydiagnosticerede og tidligere diagnosticerede børn med IBD, og viser at Crohns sygdom dominerer blandt nydiagnosticerede (64 %), mens aldersfordelingen er kraftigt koncentreret i 10–17-årsgruppen (89 % og 93 %).
